expectations.text: Identifies inline data injection or paste-based patterns in exercise prompts
expectations.evidence: The audit report marks D3 as CLEAN, stating 'No instances of Read demo-data.md or similar patterns.' However, Prompt 3 (lines 351-368 of the lesson) contains a clear paste-based data injection pattern: the student is instructed to paste fabricated reconciliation items ('3 timing differences totalling $5,200', '1 bank charge of $150 not posted to GL', '1 unidentified item of $780') directly into a prompt. This is inline data injection — fabricated numbers hardcoded into a prompt for the student to copy-paste. The skill only checked for file-reference patterns (Read demo-data.md) and missed the paste-based variant.

The skill correctly identified that this lesson uses slash commands (/reconciliation, /journal-entry, /variance-analysis, /income-statement, /sox-testing) rather than skills, so skill-name additions are not applicable. claims.evidence: Line 236 states 'volume was on plan, but average selling price fell 7% due to promotional discounting in one product line' — these specific percentages and explanations are fabricated agent output not seeded by the practice data prompt. The audit report did not flag this as a separate D1 instance, only identifying the Day 3 reconciliation table.

suggestions.assertion: Identifies inline data injection or paste-based patterns in exercise prompts
suggestions.reason: This assertion correctly caught a real miss: the skill only checked for file-reference injection (Read demo-data.md) but missed paste-based injection in Prompt 3. The assertion is well-designed and discriminating — it catches a genuine blind spot in the skill's D3 detection logic.

No assertion checks whether the skill catches ALL instances of fabricated agent output in the narrative. The skill found the Day 3 reconciliation table (lines 212-219) but missed the Day 5 variance explanation (line 236: 'volume was on plan, but average selling price fell 7% due to promotional discounting in one product line') which is also fabricated output not seeded by the practice data. An assertion like 'Identifies all fabricated agent output instances, not just the most prominent one' would catch incomplete D1 scanning.

eval_feedback.overall: The eval set is well-designed. The terminology assertion (expectation 1) and the Ch17/Ch18+ distinction (expectation 5) are both discriminating — they test whether the skill understands the domain-specific exception rather than applying a blanket rule. The data injection assertion (expectation 2) correctly caught a real skill deficiency. Consider adding coverage for completeness of D1 detection across the full lesson narrative.
